title: Refine, Don't Reinvent: RASA-Bench for Source-Grounded Hindi Prose Refinement
abstract: arXiv:2611.29750v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: For a producer of Hindi creative prose, drafting is cheap and editing is not: a machine-written episode, story, or essay reads as under-written and flat, laced with translationese, and it sometimes quietly alters what the source says. RASA-Bench targets that editing task across three Hindi prose forms, measuring how well a model refines an under-written AI draft, a task distinct from writing from scratch. Across 2,050 drafts and eight refiners (16,400 rewrites), a four-layer protocol credits a rewrite only after it passes a faithfulness check against its own source, then ranks the survivors by holistic editorial preference through per-form Bradley-Terry fits whose centered coefficients are standardized before equal-weight averaging. Staying faithful proves to be a decisive test that behaves differently by form: gate-failure rates range from 9.1% on short stories to 29.5% on audio fiction, and the drift that disqualifies a rewrite shift

translated_title: 精炼而非重造：RASA-Bench——基于源文本的印地语散文润色基准
translated_abstract: 对于印地语创意散文的创作者而言，起草很容易，编辑却不然：机器撰写的剧集、故事或文章读起来内容单薄、平淡无奇，夹杂着翻译腔，有时还会悄然改变源文本的内容。RASA-Bench 针对三种印地语散文形式中的这一编辑任务，衡量模型对内容单薄的 AI 草稿进行润色的能力——这是一项不同于从零开始写作的任务。该基准涵盖 2,050 份草稿和八个润色模型（共 16,400 次重写），采用四层评估协议：重写文本必须首先通过与源文本的忠实性检查，随后依据整体编辑偏好，通过逐形式拟合的 Bradley-Terry 模型（其中心化系数在等权平均前经过标准化）对通过者进行排名。事实证明，保持忠实是一项决定性考验，且在不同文体上表现各异：门控失败率从短篇小说的 9.1% 到有声小说的 29.5% 不等，而使重写被淘汰的偏移……
tldr: RASA-Bench 提出了一个针对印地语散文润色任务的新基准，通过忠实性门控加 Bradley-Terry 编辑偏好排名的四层评估协议，衡量模型在不偏离源文本前提下改进单薄 AI 草稿的能力，发现忠实性测试在短篇小说与有声小说等不同文体上的淘汰率差异显著。
en_tdlr: RASA-Bench introduces a benchmark for source-grounded Hindi prose refinement, using a four-layer protocol combining faithfulness gating with Bradley-Terry editorial preference rankings over 2,050 drafts and eight refiners, revealing that faithfulness failure rates vary sharply across prose forms.
